c74object.name: evi.backverb~
c74object.digest: Ursa Major reverb unit with saturating feedback
c74object.description: A strange reverb-like effect, based on Christopher Moore's legendary 1978 Ursa Major Space Station algorithm. This is not an attempt to model the 1970's digital hardware, but more of a trope on it, although it does sound very close to the original with the right settings. Nonlinearities and trap filters have been added, much as you might find in an analog delay, as well as different modulation, interpolation, smoothing and filtering modifications. Also cheap on CPU.

method.name: pattrstorage
method.digest: In left inlet, pattrstorage messages to evi.backverb~
method.description: Prepending the word 'pattrstorage' allows you to send any message 'pattrstorage' understands to the internal pattrstorage object - you can recieve pattrstorage output via the far right outlet.

attribute.name: drywet
attribute.description: Dry/Wet mix of direct signal and reverberated signal. Dry is 0, completely wet is 1.

attribute.name: feedback
attribute.description: Linear amplitude, but does not act like it. Think of this as the amount of feedback potential in the system, depending on other attributes.

attribute.name: feedbackdamphigh
attribute.description: The high damping amount of the post feedback trap filters at the Hz point of @feedbackhzhigh. The higher the values the more damping takes place, the lower the values the more feedback will recirculate.

attribute.name: feedbackdamplow
attribute.description: The low damping amount of the post feedback trap filters at the Hz point of @feedbackhzlow. The higher the values the more damping takes place, the lower the values the more feedback will recirculate.

attribute.name: feedbackhzhigh
attribute.description: The high feedback attenuation point in Hz of the post feedback trap filters.

attribute.name: feedbackhzlow
attribute.description: The low feedback attenuation point in Hz of the post feedback trap filters.

attribute.name: feedbacknonlinear
attribute.description: The nonlinearity in the feedback path of the reverb. 0=Adaa2 (2nd order antiderivative antialiasing) tanh-like saturation, 1=same but 2x oversampled, 2=same but 4x oversampled.

attribute.name: inputhzhigh
attribute.description: Lowpass the audio input at specified Hz

attribute.name: inputhzlow
attribute.description: Highpass the audio input at specified Hz

attribute.name: modulationdepth
attribute.description: The closer to zero this value is, the more feedback recirculation will be allowed to occur. The higher the values the more movement in the sound. This can be a really useful parameter to be in control of feedback surges.

attribute.name: modulationduty
attribute.description: The duty of the triangle portion of the modulation LFO (if selected).

attribute.name: modulationrate
attribute.description: The slower the rate (lower values) the more the feedback can build, the higher the rate the more in control the feedback can be kept.

attribute.name: modulationshape
attribute.description: Morph modulation LFO between triangle..sine shapes 0..1.

attribute.name: modulationskew
attribute.description: Exponentially skew the modulation LFO shape.

attribute.name: outputnonlinear
attribute.description: The cubic nonlinear shape at the end of the reverb chain. 0=Adaa1 (1st order antiderivative antialiasing), 1=Adaa2 (2nd order antiderivative antialiasing).

c74object.discussion: For more information about other reverbs in evieve, see the 'evieve reverb' tab of the helpfile.
